# Data Acquisition

# Task 1a: Data Acquisition - State Electricity Profiles
```{r}
# Load required packages
library(tidyverse)
library(stringr)
library(httr2)
library(rvest)
library(readxl)
library(fs)
library(scales)
```

# Data Acquisition - State Electricity Profiles

The data was acquired from the EIA website that combined all information into one data set on all 50 states, including CO₂ emissions, primary energy sources, electricity prices, and total electricity generation. 

```{r}
get_eia_sep <- function(state, abbr) {
  library(tidyverse)
  library(stringr)
  library(httr2)
  library(rvest)

  state_formatted <- str_to_lower(state) |>
    str_replace_all("\\s", "")

  dir_name <- file.path("data", "mp02")
  file_name <- file.path(dir_name, state_formatted)

  dir.create(dir_name, showWarnings = FALSE,
             recursive = TRUE)

  if (!file.exists(file_name)) {
    BASE_URL <- "https://www.eia.gov"

    RESPONSE <- request(BASE_URL) |>
      req_url_path(
        "electricity",
        "state",
        state_formatted
      ) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` =
          "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>
      req_perform(file_name)

    resp_check_status(RESPONSE)
  }

  TABLE <- read_html(file_name) |>
    html_element("table") |>
    html_table() |>
    mutate(Item = str_to_lower(Item))

  if ("U.S. rank" %in% colnames(TABLE)) {
    TABLE <- TABLE |>
      rename(Rank = `U.S. rank`)
  }

  CO2_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "carbon dioxide (lbs/mwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()

  PRIMARY <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "primary energy source") |>
    pull(Rank)

  RATE <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "average retail price (cents/kwh)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    as.numeric()

  GENERATION_MWh <- TABLE |>
    filter(Item == "net generation (megawatthours)") |>
    pull(Value) |>
    str_replace_all(",", "") |>
    as.numeric()

  data.frame(
    CO2_MWh = CO2_MWh,
    primary_source = PRIMARY,
    electricity_price_MWh = RATE * 10,
    generation_MWh = GENERATION_MWh,
    state = state,
    abbreviation = abbr
  )
}

EIA_SEP_REPORT <- map2(
  state.name,
  state.abb,
  get_eia_sep
) |>
  list_rbind()
```


# Data Acquisition - Energy Consumption

```{r}
load_ntd_energy <- function(){
  library(readxl)
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)
  

  DATA_DIR <- file.path("data", "mp02")
  dir.create(DATA_DIR, showWarnings=FALSE, recursive=TRUE)

  NTD_ENERGY_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_energy.xlsx")

  if(!file.exists(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)){
    library(httr2)
  
    request("https://www.transit.dot.gov/sites/fta.dot.gov/files/2026-09/2025%20Energy%20Consumption_260806.xlsx") |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0") |> 
      req_perform(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)
  }
  
  if(file.info(NTD_ENERGY_FILE)$size < 1e4){
        cat("I was unable to download the NTD Energy File. Please try again.\n")
        stop("Download failed. Please delete corrupted file and try again.")
    }

  to_numeric_fill_0 <- function(x){
    x <- if_else(x == "-", NA, x)
    replace_na(as.numeric(x), 0)
  }

  read_excel(NTD_ENERGY_FILE) |> 
    select(-c(`Reporter Type`, 
              `Reporting Module`, 
              `Gallons of Other Fuel`, 
              `Other Fuel Description`)) |>
    mutate(across(-c(`Agency Name`, 
                     `Mode`,
                     `TOS`), 
                  to_numeric_fill_0)) |>
    group_by(`NTD ID`, `Mode`, `Agency Name`) |>
    summarize(across(where(is.numeric), sum), 
              .groups = "keep") |>
    mutate(ENERGY = sum(c_across(c(where(is.numeric))))) |>
    filter(ENERGY > 0) |>
    select(-ENERGY) |>
    ungroup()
}

NTD_ENERGY <- load_ntd_energy()
```

# Transit Service Data

```{r}
load_ntd_service <- function() {
  library(httr2)
  library(tidyverse)
  library(fs)

  DATA_DIR <- file.path("data", "mp02")
  dir.create(DATA_DIR, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

  NTD_SERVICE_FILE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "2025_ntd_service.csv")

  # Download data only if the file does not exist
  if (!file.exists(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)) {

    request("https://data.transportation.gov/resource/4fir-qbim.csv") |>
      req_url_query(`$query` = paste(
        "SELECT `_5_digit_ntd_id` AS `NTD_ID`",
        "`max_agency` AS `AGENCY`",
        "`max_reporter_type` AS `reporter_type`",
        "`max_organization_type` AS `organization_type`",
        "`max_city` AS `city`",
        "`max_state` AS `state`",
        "`mode`",
        "`type_of_service`",
        "`max_primary_uza_code` as `uza_code`",
        "`max_primary_uza_name` as `uza_name`",
        "`max_primary_uza_area_sq_miles` as `uza_sq_miles`",
        "`max_primary_uza_population` as `uza_population`",
        "`max_service_area_sq_miles` as `service_area_sq_miles`",
        "`max_service_area_population` as `service_area_population`",
        "`questionable_record` as `flagged_likely_inaccurate`",
        "`sum_unlinked_passenger_trips_upt` as `total_upt`",
        "`sum_passenger_miles` WHERE caseless_one_of(`report_year`, '2025') limit 50000",
        sep = ","
      )) |>
      req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10.15; rv:149.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/149.0"
      ) |>
      req_perform(path = NTD_SERVICE_FILE)
  }

  if (file.info(NTD_SERVICE_FILE)$size < 1e4) {
    cat("I was unable to download the NTD Service File. Please try again.\n")
    stop("Download failed. Please delete corrupted file and try again.")
  }

  read_csv(
    NTD_SERVICE_FILE,
    col_types = cols(
      total_upt = col_character(),
      .default = col_guess()
    )
  ) |>
    mutate(
      total_upt = parse_number(total_upt),
      flagged_likely_inaccurate = !is.na(flagged_likely_inaccurate)
    )
}


NTD_SERVICE <- load_ntd_service()
NTD_SERVICE_FIXED <- NTD_SERVICE

```

# Data Analysis

# Calculate Total Emissions

```{r}
library(tidyverse)


service_data <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  transmute(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(as.character(NTD_ID), 5, pad = "0"),
    Mode = mode,
    state = state
  ) |>
  distinct(NTD_ID, Mode, .keep_all = TRUE)


agency_states <- NTD_SERVICE |>
  transmute(
    NTD_ID = str_pad(as.character(NTD_ID), 5, pad = "0"),
    state = state
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(state)) |>
  distinct() |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  filter(n_distinct(state) == 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  rename(agency_state = state)


energy_data <- NTD_ENERGY |>
  mutate(
    `NTD ID` = str_pad(as.character(`NTD ID`), 5, pad = "0"),
    Mode = recode(
      Mode,
      "Aerial Tramway" = "AR",
      "Alaska Railroad" = "AR",
      "Bus Rapid Transit" = "RB",
      "Cable Car" = "CC",
      "Commuter Bus" = "CB",
      "Commuter Rail" = "CR",
      "Demand Response" = "DR",
      "Ferryboat" = "FB",
      "Heavy Rail" = "HR",
      "Hybrid Rail" = "YR",
      "Inclined Plane" = "IP",
      "Light Rail" = "LR",
      "Monorail/Automated Guideway" = "MG",
      "Motor Bus" = "MB",
      "Streetcar Rail" = "SR",
      "Trolleybus" = "TB",
      "Vanpool" = "VP"
    )
  )


combined_data <- energy_data |>
  left_join(
    service_data,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID", "Mode" = "Mode")
  ) |>
  left_join(
    agency_states,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    state = coalesce(state, agency_state)
  ) |>
  select(-agency_state) |>
  left_join(
    EIA_SEP_REPORT |>
      select(abbreviation, CO2_MWh),
    by = c("state" = "abbreviation")
  )


combined_data |>
  summarize(
    total_rows = n(),
    missing_states = sum(is.na(state)),
    missing_co2 = sum(is.na(CO2_MWh)),
    duplicate_agency_modes = n() -
      n_distinct(`NTD ID`, Mode)
  )
```
The combined data including EIA electricity data, NTD energy consumption data, and NTD transit service data, contained `r format(nrow(combined_data), big.mark = ",")` records of transit agencies and transportation modes.

By calculating the CO2 fuel emissions and electricity usage, we are able to analyze  how much CO2 emissions is produced by each transit agency. Using the glimpse function, we are given an overview of the data set’s dimensions, column names, data types, and sample records.

```{r}
emissions_data <- combined_data |>
  mutate(
    
    fuel_emissions_lbs =
      coalesce(`Gallons of Diesel Fuel`, 0) * 22.45 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Gasoline`, 0) * 20.86 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Compressed Natural Gas`, 0) * 20.86 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Nat Gas`, 0) * 9.75 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Liquified Petroleum Gas`, 0) * 12.68 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Bio-Diesel`, 0) * 0 +
      coalesce(`Gallons of Ethanol`, 0) * 0 +
      coalesce(`Kilograms of Hydrogen`, 0) * 0,

    
    electricity_MWh =
      (
        coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Battery`, 0) +
        coalesce(`Kilowatt hours of Electric Propulsion`, 0)
      ) / 1000,

    
    electricity_emissions_lbs = if_else(
      electricity_MWh == 0,
      0,
      electricity_MWh * CO2_MWh
    ),

    
    total_emissions_lbs =
      fuel_emissions_lbs + electricity_emissions_lbs
  )

glimpse(emissions_data)
```

# Normalize Emissions to Transit Usage

I combined the total CO₂ emissions and total passenger usage data, which will be useful when comparing how much CO₂ each transit agency produces per passenger trip and per passenger mile.

```{r}


agency_emissions <- emissions_data |>
  group_by(`NTD ID`, `Agency Name`) |>
  summarize(
    total_emissions = if (
      all(is.na(total_emissions_lbs))
    ) NA_real_ else sum(total_emissions_lbs, na.rm = TRUE),
    missing_emissions = any(is.na(total_emissions_lbs)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agency_usage <- NTD_SERVICE_FIXED |>
  mutate(
    NTD_ID = stringr::str_pad(as.character(NTD_ID), 5, pad = "0")
  ) |>
  group_by(NTD_ID) |>
  summarize(
    total_upt = sum(total_upt, na.rm = TRUE),
    total_passenger_miles = sum(sum_passenger_miles, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

agency_efficiency <- agency_emissions |>
  left_join(
    agency_usage,
    by = c("NTD ID" = "NTD_ID")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    emissions_per_upt = if_else(
      total_upt > 0 & !missing_emissions,
      total_emissions / total_upt,
      NA_real_
    ),
    emissions_per_passenger_mile = if_else(
      total_passenger_miles > 0 & !missing_emissions,
      total_emissions / total_passenger_miles,
      NA_real_
    )
  )

glimpse(agency_efficiency)

```

By calculating CO₂ per trip and calculating CO₂ per passenger mile, we are able to compare and rank agencies from lowest to highest emissions. Based on the data, the City of Seattle is most efficient for both per trip and per passenger mile measures. The agency had about `r round(agency_efficiency |> filter(.data[["Agency Name"]] == "City of Seattle") |> pull(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |> first(), 4)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile and `r round(agency_efficiency |> filter(.data[["Agency Name"]] == "City of Seattle") |> pull(emissions_per_upt) |> first(), 4)` pounds of CO₂ per passenger trip.



```{r}

agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_upt >= 100000,
    total_emissions > 0,
    !is.na(emissions_per_upt)
  ) |>
  arrange(emissions_per_upt) |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    total_upt,
    emissions_per_upt
  ) |>
  head(10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Most Efficient Agencies by CO2 per UPT"
  )

agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_passenger_miles >= 100000,
    total_emissions > 0,
    !is.na(emissions_per_passenger_mile)
  ) |>
  arrange(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    total_passenger_miles,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile
  ) |>
  head(10) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Most Efficient Agencies by CO2 per Passenger Mile"
  )
```


# Determine Award Winners

# Greenest Transit Agency


```{r}

greenest_agencies <- agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_passenger_miles >= 100000,
    total_emissions > 0,
    !is.na(emissions_per_passenger_mile)
  ) |>
  arrange(emissions_per_passenger_mile)


greenest_winner <- greenest_agencies |>
  slice(1)


greenest_median <- median(
  greenest_agencies$emissions_per_passenger_mile,
  na.rm = TRUE
)


greenest_winner |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Greenest Transit Agency Award"
  )


greenest_median

```

Based on the results, `r greenest_winner[["Agency Name"]][1]` was the greenest transit agency producing `r round(greenest_winner$emissions_per_passenger_mile[1], 4)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. The median agency produced `r round(greenest_median, 4)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile.


# Highest CO₂ Emissions per Passenger Mile


```{r}

least_efficient_agencies <- agency_efficiency |>
  filter(
    total_passenger_miles >= 100000,
    total_emissions > 0,
    !is.na(emissions_per_passenger_mile)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(emissions_per_passenger_mile))

least_efficient_winner <- least_efficient_agencies |>
  slice(1)

least_efficient_median <- median(
  least_efficient_agencies$emissions_per_passenger_mile,
  na.rm = TRUE
)

least_efficient_winner |>
  select(
    `Agency Name`,
    emissions_per_passenger_mile
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Highest CO₂ per Passenger Mile Award"
  )

```

`r least_efficient_winner[["Agency Name"]][1]` is the agencies with the highest CO₂ emissions per passenger mile, producing about `r round(least_efficient_winner |> pull(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |> first(), 4)` pounds CO₂ per passenger mile compared to the median of `r round(least_efficient_median, 4)` pounds CO₂ per passenger mile among other agencies in the data set. 

# Press Release 

# 2025 annual  “greenest” public transit agency award 

Introduction:

The Green Transit Alliance analyzed several public transit agencies and how they performed from an environmental standpoint using the  National Transit Database (NTD) and the Energy Information Administration. In this year's award ceremony, we gave out two awards. The first award recognized the agency with the most pollution for every mile a passenger travels, while the second award recognized the most environmentally friendly transit agency. 


# Greenest Transit Agency

This award was given based on the calculations in which we divided the total CO₂ emissions by total passenger miles for different public transit agencies and then arranged the agencies from lowest to highest emissions per passenger mile. Based on the results, `r greenest_winner[["Agency Name"]][1]` was the greenest transit agency producing `r round(greenest_winner$emissions_per_passenger_mile[1], 4)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. The median agency produced `r round(greenest_median, 4)` pounds of CO2 per passenger mile. 


```{r}
greenest_comparison <- tibble(
  Agency = c("City of Seattle", "Median Agency"),
  CO2 = c(
    greenest_winner$emissions_per_passenger_mile,
    greenest_median
  )
)

ggplot(greenest_comparison, aes(x = Agency, y = CO2)) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkgreen", width = 0.6) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(CO2, 4)),
    vjust = -0.5,
    size = 4
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1.5),
    breaks = seq(0, 1.5, 0.3)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Greenest Transit Agency Award",
    subtitle = "City of Seattle compared to the median agency",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pounds of CO2 per Passenger Mile",
    caption = "Sources: National Transit Database (NTD) and EIA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 14),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 11),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 9)
  )
```

# Highest CO₂ Emissions per Passenger Mile

```{r}
top_5_agencies <- least_efficient_agencies |>
  slice_head(n = 5)

ggplot(
  top_5_agencies,
  aes(
    x = reorder(`Agency Name`, emissions_per_passenger_mile),
    y = emissions_per_passenger_mile
  )
) +
  geom_col(fill = "darkred", width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = least_efficient_median,
    linetype = "dashed",
    color = "blue",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = round(emissions_per_passenger_mile, 2)),
    hjust = -0.2,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  coord_flip(clip = "off") +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 28),
    breaks = seq(0, 25, 5)
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Highest CO2 Emissions per Passenger Mile",
    subtitle = "Top 5 agencies with the highest emissions",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Pounds of CO2 per Passenger Mile",
    caption = "Blue dashed line = Median (1.18 lbs)\nSource: NTD (2025) and EIA"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 13, face = "bold"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10),
    plot.margin = margin(15, 25, 15, 10)
  )
```

This award was given based on the calculations in which we divided the total CO₂ emissions by total passenger miles for different public transit agencies and then arranged the agencies from highest to lowest CO₂ emissions per passenger mile. Based on the results, `r least_efficient_winner[["Agency Name"]][1]` is the agency with the highest CO2 emissions per passenger mile, producing about `r round(least_efficient_winner |> pull(emissions_per_passenger_mile) |> first(), 4)` pounds compared to the median of `r round(least_efficient_median, 4)` pounds among other agencies in the data set. 

# Conclusion:

That being said, based on the results,  `r greenest_winner[["Agency Name"]][1]` was the greenest transit agency and `r least_efficient_winner[["Agency Name"]][1]` is the agency with the highest CO2 emissions per passenger mile.
